Main limitation: its method description indicates it reuses the 75-variant PGS000077 with inverted weights, and the performance metrics shown are full-model (not PRS-only), so it is unclear how much of the discrimination is attributable to the PRS itself; this prevents a high-confidence direct-match recommendation.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). PGS000077 is preferred because its phenotyping is a direct endpoint aligned to the target (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”), it is built from a reasonably sized GWAS-significant variant set (75 SNPs), and it reports a moderate PRS-associated effect size (HR=1.45) with basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), supporting interpretability without obvious clinical leakage. However, confidence is not high because the available discrimination metrics are full-model (AUROC/C-index) rather than explicitly PGS-only, and a closely competing direct-match model exists (PGS000788) with higher full-model AUROC (0.738) and stronger HR (1.7) but with a method description that suggests a weight transformation of PGS000077 (“inverse variant weights”), creating uncertainty about comparability/implementation and whether the apparent gain reflects PRS improvement versus modeling/packaging differences.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). Among these, PGS000788 has the strongest visible discrimination/effect-size package for an aligned endpoint: phenotyping_reported is "Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia" (consistent with the target concept), with European evaluation and basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and it reports higher full-model metrics (AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.7) relative to other direct-match options (e.g., PGS000077 HR 1.45; AUROC 0.719; PGS000645 AUROC 0.578; OR 1.358; PGS002305 AUROC 0.57 in a much smaller validation). Main limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided for the leading candidates, so comparisons rely on full-model metrics and per-SD effect sizes, which are not fully comparable across studies; additionally, several high-performing models in the set target chronic lymphocytic leukemia specifically (PGS000646-000651, PGS000874, PGS003453), which are not guaranteed to be equivalent to the broader target "lymphoid leukemia".

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with phenotype fields largely consistent (some are ICD-coded M81 or time-to-event variants). PGS001273 is the best-supported choice in the visible evidence because it provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.5685 with CI; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00688) alongside basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), allowing interpretation of PRS contribution and a heritability-ceiling sanity check; several other candidates report only effect sizes or partial correlations without AUROC/R2, and the 2024–2025 models frequently lack PRS-only metrics and/or have unknown covariates. The main limitation is that PGS001273 comes from a known pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”) that domain knowledge flags as potentially less reliable for external generalization, and a competing osteoporosis-specific time-to-event sibling (PGS001274) has slightly higher PGS-only AUROC/R2; however, the time-to-event endpoint is a noted warning signal and does not clearly dominate for generic osteoporosis risk, leaving residual ambiguity and keeping confidence moderate rather than high.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, with some variants targeting ICD10 M81 (osteoporosis without pathological fracture) and one time-to-event formulation (PGS001274). The strongest visible structural signal is method: PGS005155 uses PRS-CSx (a cross-ancestry extension), with a genome-wide variant count (908,465) and matched East Asian evaluation; it also reports an effect size (β=1.1443), which is stronger than the other effect-size-only osteoporosis candidates shown (e.g., PGS002768 OR=1.31; Commun Biol 2024 models OR~1.18–1.33) and avoids relying on full-model AUROC. However, the evidence remains limited/conflicted because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for most candidates (including PGS005155), while the only models with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² (PGS001273/PGS001274) come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper that domain guidance warns can generalize poorly; additionally, the β effect size is not directly comparable to per-SD OR/HR across studies. With these gaps, no single model is unequivocally best-supported from the provided metadata, so confidence is low.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, with some being closely related ICD10 sub-encodings (e.g., M81) or time-to-event variants. Framework-origin scores (PGS001273/PGS001274 from the “across 813 traits” pan-trait UKB framework; PGS001883/PGS002095 from the UKB “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework) are penalized per the provided domain guidance when other acceptable direct-match alternatives exist. Among the remaining direct-match set, PGS004810 (PRSmixPlus) has the strongest methodological signal (explicit multi-score/mixture integration) and very large variant count (1,876,917), and it reports an isolated PRS contribution metric (incremental R2=0.022) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) in a non-UKB cohort context (AllofUs), supporting better generalizability than UKB-only framework scores. Key limitation: many candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2 and several report only effect sizes (OR/β) with limited detail, making cross-candidate performance ranking uncertain; additionally, some 2024 Commun Biol candidates have unknown covariates, lowering comparability. Therefore, a direct match exists but evidence is insufficient for a clearly dominant, conflict-free choice.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported. Among them, several are from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001273/PGS001274 from the “813 traits” sparse framework; PGS001883/PGS002095 from “Portability of 245 polygenic scores”), which domain guidance flags as systematically weaker than disease-focused alternatives when such alternatives exist. The 2024 Commun Biol cluster (PGS004490/PGS004495/PGS004560/PGS004565) is coherent on endpoint (osteoporosis or M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture) and uses methodologically strong multi-score aggregation (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which domain knowledge prioritizes over single-score methods; within that cluster, PGS004565 targets ‘Osteoporosis’ (not the M81 subtype) and has the largest reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.328222), providing the strongest available PRS-discrimination signal among those siblings. Main limitation: most non-framework candidates (including PGS004565) lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), covariates are ‘Unknown’ for the chosen model, and competing candidates also have plausible support (e.g., PGS002768 reports OR=1.31 with EUR eval; PGS001274 has slightly higher incremental AUROC but is from a pan-trait framework and is time-to-event). This leaves residual uncertainty, so the direct-match recommendation is best-available but not high-confidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait osteoporosis by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. The strongest structural signal in this pool is method: multi-score aggregation methods are strongly preferred when available. Among the aggregation candidates, PGS004565 (RFDiseasemetaPRS) targets Osteoporosis with a direct diagnosis endpoint, EUR development/evaluation, and reports an OR per SD of 1.328 (moderate effect-size support). Competing candidates are either (i) pan-trait/portability framework scores (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’ PGS001273/PGS001274; ‘Portability of 245’ PGS001883/PGS002095) which domain guidance flags as systematically weaker archetypes despite having some PRS-only metrics, or (ii) single-score shrinkage approaches with weaker or less informative evidence in this context (e.g., PGS002768 OR 1.31; PRS-CS/PRS-CSx EAS-only models PGS005146/PGS005155 without comparable AUC/R2 here; PRSmix/PRSmixPlus PGS004809/PGS004810 report incremental R2 but on small validation n=9,462). Limitation: for the selected Commun Biol 2024 family (PGS004490/PGS004495/PGS004560/PGS004565), covariates are listed as Unknown and only effect sizes (no PRS-only AUROC/R2) are available, and multiple near-identical siblings exist, preventing a clearly high-confidence best choice; hence the direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the evidence is heterogeneous and often lacks PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (many provide only OR/β without AUROC/R²). The pan-trait UKB snpnet models (PGS001273/PGS001274) do report PGS-only AUROC/R², but their publication context is an explicitly pan-trait framework ('across 813 traits'), which domain knowledge flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused alternatives and as vulnerable to covariate-driven full-model AUROC (incremental AUROC and PGS-only R² are small). Among non-framework, endpoint-faithful options, PGS005155 (PRS-CSx) is methodologically strong (cross-ancestry joint modeling) and directly targets osteoporosis with basic covariates (age, sex) and a large EAS evaluation (n=58,611), making it the best-supported single candidate on structure/transportability within the provided metadata. Main limitation: performance reporting is not directly comparable (only a β effect size; no PRS-only AUROC/R²), and there is meaningful competition from other genome-wide approaches with similar endpoint alignment (e.g., PGS002768 PRS-CS with OR=1.31; PGS004565 RFDiseasemetaPRS OR=1.328; PGS004810 PRSmixPlus incremental R²=0.022), so a clearly strong recommendation is not supported from the visible evidence alone.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) at the concept level, but the evidence is heterogeneous and often non-comparable: several are from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001273/PGS001274: “across 813 traits”; PGS001883/PGS002095: “Portability of 245 polygenic scores”), many newer models report only effect sizes without PRS-only AUROC/R² (e.g., PGS002768, PGS004495, PGS004565) or have unknown covariates (PGS004495/PGS004565), and the East Asian-only models (PGS005146/PGS005155) are ancestry-specific with no comparative PRS-only metrics. PGS001273 is selected because it is an exact osteoporosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported/trait_reported both “Osteoporosis”), provides explicit PRS-comparable performance (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.5685; PGS R² (no covariates)=0.00688) and incremental AUROC (0.00477), enabling a sanity-check consistent with the provided heritability guidance; competing candidates largely lack PRS-only metrics or are endpoint variants (time-to-event / M81 subtype). Main limitation: PGS001273 is from a pan-trait sparse framework (snpnet with only 316 variants), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused alternatives, but the context does not provide a clearly better-supported disease-focused osteoporosis PRS with comparable PRS-only metrics to justify a higher-confidence choice.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait osteoporosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported explicitly osteoporosis or an ICD-derived osteoporosis subtype). The strongest structural signal in this pool is the presence of a cross-ancestry joint-modeling method (PRS-CSx) with a genome-wide variant set: PGS005155 (PRS-CSx; 908,465 variants; GWAS EAS+EUR; EVAL EAS; n=58,611). This aligns with the domain guidance favoring method family/capabilities (including cross-ancestry extensions) and large genome-wide models when endpoint fidelity is comparable. However, evidence is limited/conflicted because most candidates (including PGS005155) lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²); PGS005155 reports only a beta effect size without clear per-SD OR/HR, and several alternatives either provide weak-to-moderate effect-size evidence (e.g., PGS002768 OR=1.31 in EUR) or come from framework/portability contexts (813-traits snpnet; 245-scores portability) with known generalization concerns. Given missing comparable performance metrics across the top contenders and mixed study archetypes, the selection is not clearly best-supported enough for a high-quality designation.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) at the concept level (trait_efo=osteoporosis and phenotyping_reported indicates osteoporosis or an ICD10-aligned subtype such as M81). The strongest structural signal in this set is the presence of a multi-score aggregation method (domain knowledge Property 1), which is represented by the RFDiseasemetaPRS models; among these, PGS004565 targets generic osteoporosis (not the narrower M81 subtype) and reports the strongest available effect size in that family (OR=1.328222), exceeding the corresponding LDpred2 siblings (OR~1.18–1.20). However, the selection remains sub-optimal because most non-framework, non-sparse candidates here lack PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), covariates are listed as unknown for the chosen model family, and the only models with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² (PGS001273/PGS001274) are from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework that domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly; this creates unresolved comparability limitations and prevents a high-confidence best-pick.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer), with endpoint-faithful phenotypes such as “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Incident testicular cancer.” Among the coherent Cancer PRSweb cluster (PGS000595–PGS000604), PGS000604 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has the strongest reported evaluation metrics within that family (full-model AUROC 0.703 [0.659–0.745], Nagelkerke’s pseudo-R² 0.0882, and OR per SD 2.106 [1.729–2.565]) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and consistent EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry. The main limitation is that most candidates (including PGS000604) report only full-model metrics rather than clearly PRS-only metrics, making cross-model ranking less reliable; additionally, an alternative framework/pan-trait score (PGS001164, snpnet) provides explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework context per the domain guidance, and PGS000796 shows very high full-model metrics in a risk-factor integration setting without PRS-only isolation, so neither cleanly resolves the comparability gap. Therefore a direct match exists, but the evidence does not support a single unequivocally high-quality winner.

All listed candidates are direct matches for the target trait (testicular carcinoma) via trait_efo and phenotype fields (e.g., "Malignant neoplasm of testis" or "Testicular cancer"). Among the coherent Cancer PRSweb sibling set with identical/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs) and consistent EUR ancestry, PGS000604 shows the strongest visible validation performance (full-model AUROC 0.703 with CI 0.659–0.745; highest full-model R2 0.0882; OR per SD 2.106) and is closely supported by its sibling PGS000602 (AUROC 0.698; R2 0.0839). Competing candidates include PGS001164 (a pan-trait UKB "813 traits" framework score, penalized by domain guidance despite reporting PGS-only AUROC/R2) and PGS000796 (very high full-model AUROC/R2 but with no PRS-only metrics and an incident-only endpoint plus broader risk-factor integration context, making the performance less directly comparable). Main limitation: most PRSweb models report only full-model metrics (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so ranking relies on within-family comparability and effect sizes rather than clean PRS-only discrimination evidence.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (testicular carcinoma) with endpoint-faithful phenotypes (e.g., "Malignant neoplasm of testis" or "Incident testicular cancer"). Among the Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet) cluster, PGS000604 shows the strongest reported validation in a comparable European setting with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs): highest full-model AUROC (0.703; 95% CI 0.659–0.745), highest/near-highest full-model Nagelkerke R² (0.0882), and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 2.106; 95% CI 1.729–2.565) versus the closely competing sibling PGS000602 (AUROC 0.698; R² 0.0839; OR 2.055). A key limitation is that these PRSweb models report only full-model discrimination (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), so metric comparability across studies is imperfect; additionally, other direct-match candidates (e.g., PGS000796, PGS001164) have much higher reported full-model metrics but come from different study archetypes/endpoints, making it unclear whether those values reflect PRS-only signal. Given the coherent disease-focused PRSweb cluster and PGS000604’s consistent within-cluster edge, it is the best-supported direct-match choice with moderate confidence.

All 11 candidates are direct matches to Parkinson disease at the trait/efo level, but several are progression/dementia endpoints (PGS000056 cognitive decline, PGS000211 motor decline, PGS000777 Parkinson’s disease dementia) rather than generic PD risk/status, making them less aligned for a generic “parkinson disease” target. Among the models with phenotyping_reported explicitly “Parkinson’s disease,” PGS000903 provides the strongest visible performance evidence (full_model AUROC=0.692; reports R²=0.054 and OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25) and uses only basic covariates (PCs, age, sex) with a large, disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context (same Lancet Neurol study family as PGS000902; multi-cohort development listed). The main limitation is that the reported metrics appear to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), so comparability across models is imperfect; other candidates (e.g., PGS001774 AUROC=0.8) likely benefit from heavier non-genetic covariates including family history and multiple established risk factors, making that AUC less informative for PRS-only quality. Given these constraints, PGS000903 is the best-supported direct-match choice from the available metadata, but confidence is limited by lack of clearly isolated PGS-only discrimination metrics across the candidate set.
